New Hanover County Superior Court: Complete Guide

Contact Information

  • Address: 316 Princess Street, PO Box 2023, Wilmington, NC 28402
  • Phone: 910-772-6600
  • Website: https://www.nccourts.gov/locations/new-hanover-county/new-hanover-county-courthouse
  • Hours: Monday-Friday, 8 AM–5 PM (Closed weekends)

Overview of New Hanover County Courts

New Hanover County operates two main courts:

  • District Court: Handles misdemeanors, traffic violations, and civil cases up to $25,000
  • Superior Court: Manages felony criminal cases and civil matters exceeding $25,000

Both courts are housed in the New Hanover County Courthouse in Wilmington.

History and Jurisdiction

Established in 1892, the New Hanover County Superior Court has evolved into a cornerstone of justice in the region. The court has general jurisdiction over:

  • Criminal cases (misdemeanors to felonies)
  • Civil disputes (contracts, personal injury, property)
  • Family law matters (divorce, custody, adoption)

Court Calendar and Case Lookup

Accessing the Court Calendar

Online Options:

  • The county publishes daily updated calendars for both District and Superior Court
  • Search by party name or case number
  • Create an account to receive email/text notifications for calendar changes

In-Person Options:

  • View printed daily calendars posted near the clerk's offices

Court Calendar Details Include:

  • Case numbers
  • Party names
  • Hearing types
  • Scheduled times
  • Courtroom assignments

Court Case Lookup System

Visit the official New Hanover County courts website to search cases by:

  • Case number
  • Names of involved parties
  • Other identifying information

New Hanover County Clerk of Court

The Clerk's office handles:

  • Filing and maintaining court documents
  • Processing marriage licenses
  • Estate administration
  • Record certification

Contact the Clerk's office directly for questions about court procedures or accessing records.

Public Records and Legal Services

Accessing Arrest Records

Visit the New Hanover County website's public records section to find:

  • Names of arrested individuals
  • Arrest dates
  • Charges filed
  • Related court dates

Marriage Services

The county magistrate can:

  • Perform marriages
  • Issue marriage licenses (requires identification, completed application, and payment of fees)

Court Personnel

Judges

New Hanover County judges preside over various cases, from civil disputes to criminal trials, ensuring fair and impartial decisions.

Court Staff

A dedicated team supports the efficient functioning of the court through administrative assistance and procedural guidance.

Technology and Innovation

The court has embraced digital transformation through:

  • Digitized record systems
  • Online case management
  • Electronic filing options
  • Online payment systems

These improvements have enhanced efficiency, convenience, and transparency.

Community Outreach

The court actively engages with the community through:

  • Educational workshops and seminars
  • Public forums on the justice system
  • Alternative dispute resolution programs (mediation and arbitration)

Using the Court Calendar Effectively

  • Regular Checks: Frequently review the calendar as dates may change
  • Case Status: Monitor any actions taken on your case
  • Preparation: Arrange time off work, transportation, and childcare in advance
  • Witness Coordination: Notify witnesses of appearance dates
  • Evidence Management: Ensure exhibits are ready for presentation

FAQs

How do I file a case in New Hanover County Superior Court? Gather relevant documents, complete the necessary legal forms, pay the required filing fees, and submit everything to the court clerk's office. Consulting an attorney is recommended.

Can I access court records online? Yes, most court records are available through the digitalized system, though some sensitive information may be restricted.

How are judges appointed? Judges are either appointed by the governor or elected through judicial elections based on legal qualifications, experience, and ethical standing.

What alternative dispute resolution options are available? The court encourages mediation (facilitated negotiation) and arbitration (binding third-party decision) as alternatives to traditional court proceedings.

Is the online court calendar publicly accessible? Yes, the calendar is available for free public viewing.

How often is the online calendar updated? The system is updated daily as changes occur, providing the most current scheduling information.
